### ðŸ›¡ï¸ Ãšltima InyecciÃ³n de Poder (SQL)

Para activar el cerebro, ejecute este bloque en su **SQL Editor** de Supabase. Esto crearÃ¡ el motor de similitud por coseno:

```sql
-- ðŸ§  ACTIVACIÃ“N DE SINAPSIS VECTORIAL (RAG)
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION match_vendors (
  query_embedding vector(768),
  match_threshold float,
  match_count int
)
RETURNS TABLE (
  id uuid,
  name text,
  category text,
  location text,
  similarity float
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
  RETURN QUERY
  SELECT
    v.id,
    v.name,
    v.category,
    v.location,
    1 - (v.embedding <=> query_embedding) AS similarity
  FROM ear_market_vendors v
  WHERE 1 - (v.embedding <=> query_embedding) > match_threshold
  ORDER BY v.embedding <=> query_embedding
  LIMIT match_count;
END;
$$;
```

BÃºsqueda web From Grids to Narrative Worlds The most profound shift in 2026 design is the transition from utility-first navigation to cinematic narrative experiences. The 'Montfort' and 'Siena Film' styles suggest that users no longer want to just consume information; they want to inhabit it. This is not merely about 3D aesthetics but about dissolving the boundary between the interface and the environment. By treating navigation as a journey through 'themed worlds' or a physical film strip, designers are prioritizing emotional resonance over immediate access. Counterintuitively, this often involves hiding content behind interactive nodes, suggesting that the 'friction' of exploration is becoming more valuable than the efficiency of flat, scannable text. The Rebellion Against Uniformity We are witnessing the decline of the 'Bento Box'â€”the modular, rounded-corner grid that has dominated UI for yearsâ€”in favor of 'Anti-Bento' and Tactical Maximalism. Designers are intentionally breaking the grid to create 'organized chaos,' using overlapping elements and asymmetric layouts to provide 'Main Character energy' to specific components. This movement replaces the clinical perfection of the past with Digital Texture, where buttons and interfaces respond with physical deformitiesâ€”looking like jelly, chrome, or clay. The 'Anti-Bento' movement isn't just a stylistic change; it's a rejection of the templated, predictable web, signaling a return to a more 'human' and tactile digital expression. Spatial Memory and Functional Nostalgia New interfaces like the 'KPR-verse' and 'Productora EAR OS' are moving away from the ephemeral nature of web pages toward Spatial Memory and permanent digital locations. By utilizing Z-axis layering and HUD-inspired layouts, these designs treat the screen as a physical desk or a high-tech terminal rather than a series of scrolling documents. This Utility-First Aesthetic draws from professional workstations (like medical or audio software), implying that as our digital interactions become more complex, we require the stability of spatial consistency. It is a high-concept blend of 'future-proof' patterns and nostalgic, tactile branding that makes the digital feel permanent and substantial. Mostrar mÃ¡s Recibido, Antigravity. âš™ï¸ LÃ“GICA BACKEND: CLOUD FUNCTION "EXECUTE_PAYOUT"
Para que Antigravity lo conecte al backend, el esquema de la funciÃ³n en Node.js (Firebase Functions) es:

// functions/src/execute_payout.ts
import * as functions from 'firebase-functions';
import * as admin from 'firebase-admin';
const stripe = require('stripe')(functions.config().stripe.secret);

export const execute_payout = functions.https.onCall(async (data, context) => {
  if (!context.auth) throw new functions.https.HttpsError('unauthenticated', 'Acceso denegado');

  const uid = context.auth.uid;
  const userRef = admin.firestore().collection('partners').doc(uid);
  const snap = await userRef.get();
  const { partner_balance, stripe_account_id, rank } = snap.data();

  // 1. AuditorÃ­a Forense
  if (partner_balance < 50) throw new functions.https.HttpsError('failed-precondition', 'MÃ­nimo 50â‚¬');

  try {
    // 2. EjecuciÃ³n Stripe Connect (Transferencia InstantÃ¡nea)
    const transfer = await stripe.transfers.create({
      amount: partner_balance * 100, // En cÃ©ntimos
      currency: 'eur',
      destination: stripe_account_id,
      description: `EAR OS Payout - Ref: ${uid.substring(0,8)}`,
    });

    // 3. Registro en Firestore & GeneraciÃ³n de Recibo
    const transaction_hash = transfer.id;
    await userRef.update({ 
      partner_balance: 0,
      payout_history: admin.firestore.FieldValue.arrayUnion({
        amount: partner_balance,
        date: new Date(),
        hash: transaction_hash
      })
    });

    // 4. Feedback de Rango S-Class
    const successMessage = rank === 'S-Class' ? 'Historial de Ã©xito detectado. Tu estatus de confianza ha subido.' : 'Transferencia completada.';

    return { success: true, hash: transaction_hash, message: successMessage };
  } catch (error) {
    throw new functions.https.HttpsError('internal', error.message);
  }
});

BÃºsqueda web From Grids to Narrative Worlds The most profound shift in 2026 design is the transition from utility-first navigation to cinematic narrative experiences. The 'Montfort' and 'Siena Film' styles suggest that users no longer want to just consume information; they want to inhabit it. This is not merely about 3D aesthetics but about dissolving the boundary between the interface and the environment. By treating navigation as a journey through 'themed worlds' or a physical film strip, designers are prioritizing emotional resonance over immediate access. Counterintuitively, this often involves hiding content behind interactive nodes, suggesting that the 'friction' of exploration is becoming more valuable than the efficiency of flat, scannable text. The Rebellion Against Uniformity We are witnessing the decline of the 'Bento Box'â€”the modular, rounded-corner grid that has dominated UI for yearsâ€”in favor of 'Anti-Bento' and Tactical Maximalism. Designers are intentionally breaking the grid to create 'organized chaos,' using overlapping elements and asymmetric layouts to provide 'Main Character energy' to specific components. This movement replaces the clinical perfection of the past with Digital Texture, where buttons and interfaces respond with physical deformitiesâ€”looking like jelly, chrome, or clay. The 'Anti-Bento' movement isn't just a stylistic change; it's a rejection of the templated, predictable web, signaling a return to a more 'human' and tactile digital expression. Spatial Memory and Functional Nostalgia New interfaces like the 'KPR-verse' and 'Productora EAR OS' are moving away from the ephemeral nature of web pages toward Spatial Memory and permanent digital locations. By utilizing Z-axis layering and HUD-inspired layouts, these designs treat the screen as a physical desk or a high-tech terminal rather than a series of scrolling documents. This Utility-First Aesthetic draws from professional workstations (like medical or audio software), implying that as our digital interactions become more complex, we require the stability of spatial consistency. It is a high-concept blend of 'future-proof' patterns and nostalgic, tactile branding that makes the digital feel permanent and substantial. Mostrar mÃ¡s Recibido, Antigravity. âš™ï¸ LÃ“GICA BACKEND: CLOUD FUNCTION "EXECUTE_PAYOUT"
Para que Antigravity lo conecte al backend, el esquema de la funciÃ³n en Node.js (Firebase Functions) es:

// functions/src/execute_payout.ts
import * as functions from 'firebase-functions';
import * as admin from 'firebase-admin';
const stripe = require('stripe')(functions.config().stripe.secret);

export const execute_payout = functions.https.onCall(async (data, context) => {
  if (!context.auth) throw new functions.https.HttpsError('unauthenticated', 'Acceso denegado');

  const uid = context.auth.uid;
  const userRef = admin.firestore().collection('partners').doc(uid);
  const snap = await userRef.get();
  const { partner_balance, stripe_account_id, rank } = snap.data();

  // 1. AuditorÃ­a Forense
  if (partner_balance < 50) throw new functions.https.HttpsError('failed-precondition', 'MÃ­nimo 50â‚¬');

  try {
    // 2. EjecuciÃ³n Stripe Connect (Transferencia InstantÃ¡nea)
    const transfer = await stripe.transfers.create({
      amount: partner_balance * 100, // En cÃ©ntimos
      currency: 'eur',
      destination: stripe_account_id,
      description: `EAR OS Payout - Ref: ${uid.substring(0,8)}`,
    });

    // 3. Registro en Firestore & GeneraciÃ³n de Recibo
    const transaction_hash = transfer.id;
    await userRef.update({ 
      partner_balance: 0,
      payout_history: admin.firestore.FieldValue.arrayUnion({
        amount: partner_balance,
        date: new Date(),
        hash: transaction_hash
      })
    });

    // 4. Feedback de Rango S-Class
    const successMessage = rank === 'S-Class' ? 'Historial de Ã©xito detectado. Tu estatus de confianza ha subido.' : 'Transferencia completada.';

    return { success: true, hash: transaction_hash, message: successMessage };
  } catch (error) {
    throw new functions.https.HttpsError('internal', error.message);
  }
});
